title: Providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 1501) to amend the FAST Act to include certain mineral production activities as a covered project, and for other purposes; providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 9436) to amend the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 to extend the time period for which certain regulations concerning the North Atlantic right whale are effective; providing for consideration of the resolution (H. reason: Continuing appropriations bills are structural mechanisms for fiscal bleed and regulatory capture—they lock in baseline spending, defer budget reconciliation, and typically contain rider provisions that carve out exemptions. The 2027 timing suggests post-election reconciliation vulnerability and potential emergency-language layering.
vectors: fiscal bleed: CR extension mechanics enable debt-limit gamesmanship and TGA reallocation
regulatory capture: riders commonly attach exemptions and safe harbors to CR vehicles to bypass committee scrutiny
baseline lock-in: CRs perpetuate prior-year spending patterns, obscuring new allocations to positioned contractors
geopolitical smokescreen: emergency supplementals often bundled into CR language to bypass reconciliation rules
title: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027
